newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Treasury announces bill auction change.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Treasury announces bill auction change.

text.p: The Treasury Department announced on Tuesday that, starting with its March 26 sale of 52-week bills, awards made to Federal Reserve banks for their own accounts will be shown as additions to the announced offering amount.
Currently, awards to these accounts are within the announced offering amount.

The announcement of the details of the 52-week bill sale, scheduled for March 21, will be the first one to reflect this change. The intent is to give more complete information to market participants, Treasury said.
Treasury said there will no change in the way it reports awards to Fed banks for foreign and international monetary authorities.

Maturing amounts held by these accounts can be refunded within the announced offering amount at the average discount rate of accepted competitive bids. Purchases by these accounts that exceed the maturing amounts will continue to be shown as additions to the announced offering amount, Treasury said.
